exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $80,215.00 as of 2026-10-26 12:43:45 UTC, +0.05% over one hour and -0.14% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $79,332.00 to $80,825.00; spot sits at 59% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -2.44% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($80,222.93) is below the 72-hour average ($80,586.87). Spot is 5.38% below the seven-day high of $84,777.79 and 1.11% above the seven-day low of $79,332.00.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 1.47% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 50.6, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $20.66 billion, equal to 1.28% of the $1.61 trillion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 50 ("Neutral"), versus 59 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink BTC/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $80,228.02, 75 minutes before the spot quote and +0.02% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of BTC is essentially flat (+0.05% hour, –0.14% day) and sits near the 59 % mark of its 24‑hour range, indicating a market in equilibrium rather than a breakout to the downside, as shown in Exhibits A and B.  

2. Momentum metrics are neutral: the 14‑hour RSI is 50.6 (Exhibit D) and the seven‑day average price ($80,222.93) remains only modestly below the three‑day average ($80,586.87) (Exhibit C), suggesting no imminent bearish reversal.  

3. Liquidity remains robust with $20.66 billion traded in 24 hours (Exhibit E) and sentiment is neutral (Exhibit F), while the Chainlink feed—our execution benchmark—is within 0.02 % of spot (Exhibit G), providing a reliable price foundation for a long practice.  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is essentially flat, up only 0.05% in the last hour and down 0.14% over 24 hours, indicating a lack of upward momentum; the neutral 14‑hour RSI of 50.6 corroborates this stagnation (Ex. A, D).  

2. Volume remains modest at $20.66 billion, just 1.28% of market cap, suggesting insufficient buying pressure to break the current range; the price sits near the midpoint of the 24‑hour range (59%) and is already 5.38% below the seven‑day high (Ex. B, C, E).  

3. Sentiment has slipped from a modestly bullish 59 to a neutral 50 on the Fear & Greed Index, while the Chainlink feed—our settlement reference—shows only a 0.02% premium to spot, confirming no immediate upside bias (Ex. F, G).  

Given flat price action, weak volume, and waning sentiment, opening a short practice position is warranted.  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s claim of “flat” price ignores the decisive fact that spot sits at 59 % of the 24‑hour range, already above the midpoint, showing a bias toward the upper bound rather than stagnation (Ex. B). Moreover, the volatility of 1.47 % per day is not modest; it furnishes ample room for short‑term price swings that a short can capture (Ex. D). The Bear’s volume argument mischaracterizes $20.66 billion as modest—at 1.28 % of market cap it exceeds typical crypto turnover ratios and provides sufficient liquidity for a short entry (Ex. E). Thus, the market possesses upward pressure and adequate liquidity, undermining the short thesis. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s claim of “equilibrium” ignores the clear downward pressure evidenced by the seven‑day decline of ‑2.44 % and the fact that today’s spot sits 5.38 % below the seven‑day high (Ex. C). That gap signals a bearish bias, not stability. Moreover, the “neutral” RSI at 50.6 (Ex. D) is precisely the pivot where downside momentum typically accelerates; combined with the 24‑hour average now below the 72‑hour average (Ex. C), it shows the market is already slipping, contradicting any notion of a breakout‑free environment. Hence, the Bull’s reliance on flat hourly movement and a supposedly neutral range is outweighed by the broader downtrend data. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds a short practice position is warranted.

findings.finding: Seven‑day price decline of 2.44% and spot 5.38% below the recent high indicate bearish bias.
Fear & Greed Index fell from 59 to 50, showing waning bullish sentiment.
24‑hour volume equals only 1.28% of market cap, suggesting limited buying pressure.
RSI at 50.6 sits at the pivot where downside momentum often accelerates.
Spot sits at 59% of the 24‑hour range, modestly above the midpoint, but does not offset broader downtrend.

ruling.opinion: The exhibits show a modest multi‑day downtrend (C), weakening sentiment (F), and limited liquidity relative to market size (E). The neutral RSI (D) sits at a level where bearish pressure can build, and the price’s position within its daily range (B) offers no strong upside. Combined, these factors outweigh the Bull’s arguments for equilibrium, justifying a short practice position for the next 24 hours.
ruling.dissent: The Bull argues the price’s 59% placement in its daily range signals upward bias and that 1.28% volume is ample liquidity, but these points are outweighed by the clear multi‑day decline and deteriorating sentiment.
